problems.title: Symmetric difference
problems.question: M={a, b, c, d}, N={b, d, f}. Find M△N.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: $M\triangle N=(M\setminus N)\cup(N\setminus M)$.
steps: The common elements b, d are removed. The elements belonging to exactly one set are a, c, f.

problems.title: Percentage smaller
problems.question: City populations are 45000 and 60000. By what percentage is the first smaller than the second?
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: Percentage decrease $=(60000-45000)/60000\cdot100\%$.
steps: The difference is 15000, which is one quarter of 60000.

problems.title: Degree of a monomial
problems.question: The degree of $(-3x^2y^3)^4z^k$ is 26. Find k.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: Total degree is the sum of variable exponents: $4(2+3)+k=26$.
steps: The x, y exponents contribute 20. Subtract 20 from 26.

problems.title: Three related triangle angles
problems.question: One triangle angle is 20° greater than another and is 50% of the third. Find the smallest.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: Call the first angle t. The other two are $t-20$ and $2t$; the sum is 180°.
steps: t+(t−20)+2t=180 gives t=50°. The angles are 30°,50°,100°.

problems.title: Altitudes of an acute isosceles triangle
problems.question: The acute angle between altitudes to the equal sides of an acute isosceles triangle is 70°. Find a base angle.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: Rotating both side lines by 90° preserves their acute angle. The acute apex angle therefore is 70°.
steps: The other line-angle possibility 110° would make the triangle obtuse and is excluded. The equal base angles are(180−70)/2.

problems.title: A quotient of powers
problems.question: Evaluate $12^7\cdot54^4/(8^4\cdot36^3\cdot81^3)$.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
steps: The numerator has factors 2¹⁸3¹⁹, the denominator 2¹⁸3¹⁸. Cancellation leaves 3.

problems.title: Only one of two clubs
problems.question: Of25 pupils,60% attend math club and 40% physics club;6 attend neither. How many attend only physics club?
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: The union count is $25-6=19$. Inclusion–exclusion gives $|M\cap P|=|M|+|P|-|M\cup P|$.
steps: There are 15 in math and 10 in physics, so the overlap is 15+10−19=6. Physics only is 10−6.

problems.title: An acute angle between bisectors
problems.question: The acute angle between two internal triangle-angle bisectors is 25% less than the third angle C. Find C.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: The obtuse incentre angle is $90°+C/2$, so the acute line angle is $90°-C/2$.
steps: Set 90−C/2=(3/4)C. This gives 90=(5/4)C.

problems.title: Altitude versus angle bisector
problems.question: A triangle angle is 50°. Its altitude and internal bisector make 34°. Find the largest triangle angle.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: If the other angles are B, C, the angle between this altitude line and bisector is $|B-C|/2$.
steps: Thus B+C=130° and |B−C|=68°. The larger is(130+68)/2=99°, the other 31°. These are consistent with the given 50° angle.

problems.title: Bisector and opposite equal side
problems.question: In an obtuse isosceles triangle, a base-angle bisector makes a66° angle with one of the equal sides. Find the smallest triangle angle.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: Let each base angle be β<45°. At the bisector’s meeting point with the opposite equal side, the smaller angle is $3β/2$.
steps: Indeed the adjacent triangle has angles 180−2β and β/2, leaving 3β/2. The adjacent equal side through the bisected vertex makes only β/2<22.5°, so it cannot give 66°. Thus 3β/2=66°.

problems.title: Expand and cancel
problems.question: Simplify $x^2(1-2x)-(x^2-3x)(x+2)-(2x^2-3x^3)$.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
steps: Substitute and collect terms: x²−2x³−x³+x²+6x−2x²+3x³. Both the cubic and quadratic terms cancel.

problems.title: Mix two concentrations
problems.question: How many litres of 18% solution must be added to 12 litres of 7% solution to obtain 12% solution?
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: Conservation of solute gives $.07(12)+.18v=.12(12+v)$.

problems.title: Order expressions on the unit interval
problems.question: Order in decreasing order $A=a^3-2$, $B=(-a)^5$, $C=1-a^6$, where 0<a<1.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
steps: The intervals do not overlap. The positive expression is largest, followed by B, then A.

problems.title: Extend a median by its own length
problems.question: Median AD is extended beyond D to E with DE=AD. AB=8, AC=12, AD=9. Find perimeter ACE.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: D is midpoint of both BC and AE, so quadrilateral ABEC has bisecting diagonals and is a parallelogram. Thus $CE=AB$.
steps: CE=8 and AE=2AD=18. Add AC+CE+AE=12+8+18.

problems.title: Perimeter using a perpendicular bisector
problems.question: The perpendicular bisector of BC meets segment AC at D. AB=AC/3. What percentage of perimeter ABD is AB?
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: $DB=DC$, so $P_{ABD}=AB+AD+DB=AB+AC$.
steps: Since AC=3AB, the perimeter is 4AB. The side AB is one quarter of it.

problems.title: A final-digit calculation
problems.question: Find the final digit of $199^{2025}+7^{102}+2^{199}3^{200}$.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: Powers of 9 alternate 9,1; powers of 7 have period 4; powers of 2 have period 4; powers of 3 have period 4.
steps: 199²⁰²⁵ ends in9. Since 102≡2 mod 4,7¹⁰² ends in9. Since 199≡3 mod 4,2¹⁹⁹ ends in8, and 3²⁰⁰ ends in1. The total ends as9+9+8=26.

problems.title: Match prime-base exponents
problems.question: Natural n, m satisfy $(9^9)^n=(27^{27})^m$. Find n: m.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: The equation is $3^{18n}=3^{81m}$.
steps: Equality of the exponents gives 18n=81m. Divide by 9 and reduce the ratio.

problems.title: Dry mass stays constant
problems.question: Fresh persimmon contains 80% water and dried persimmon 40%. How much dried fruit comes from 60 kg fresh fruit if only water is lost?
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: The dry mass is $60(1-.8)=12$ kg. It is 60% of the final mass.
steps: Let final mass be W. Then .6W=12, giving W=20.

problems.title: Two descriptions of an altitude angle
problems.question: In an obtuse triangle, the acute angle between the altitudes to the sides opposite the acute angles is one quarter of the obtuse angle and 20% greater than another triangle angle. Find the smallest angle.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: Let the obtuse angle be A. The altitude-line acute angle is $180°-A=A/4$.
steps: Thus A=144° and the altitude-line angle is 36°. If36° is 20% greater than one acute angle, that angle is 36/1.2=30°. The remaining angle is 180−144−30.

problems.title: Perpendicular bisector and median
problems.question: In ABC, B-bisector BK is perpendicular to median CM. AC=10 and the perimeter is 34. Find BC.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: Place B at the origin with its bisector on the horizontal axis. Let $AB=c,BC=a$ and use $A=(c\cos t,c\sin t)$, $C=(a\cos t,-a\sin t)$.
steps: The midpoint M of AB is A/2. The perpendicularity makes CM vertical, so a cos t=(c/2)cos t. Since cos t>0, c=2a. The perimeter gives a+c=24, hence 3a=24.

problems.title: Divisible by at least one number
problems.question: How many positive integers less than 100 are divisible by 4,6 or 9?
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: Inclusion–exclusion uses the pairwise lcms 12,36,18 and the triple lcm 36.

problems.title: A parameter making a linear contradiction
problems.question: For which k is $-2kx(1-x)-(kx+1)(2x-1)+1=2k-7(kx-1)$ insoluble in x?
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: Expansion cancels the quadratic terms and leaves $(6k-2)x=2k+5$.
steps: There is no solution exactly when the x-coefficient vanishes but the constant does not. Set 6k−2=0 to obtain k=1/3. The right side is then 17/3, which is nonzero.

problems.title: Smallest group with a percentage restriction
problems.question: Girls for m strictly more than 35% and strictly less than 40% of a group. Find the smallest possible total.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: If G, N are integers, require $7N/20<G<2N/5$.
steps: For N=1,…,7 the respective open intervals are(.35,.4),(.7,.8),(1.05,1.2),(1.4,1.6),(1.75,2),(2.1,2.4),(2.45,2.8), none containing an integer. For N=8, G=3 gives 37.5%.

problems.title: A parallel through the incentre
problems.question: In triangle ABC, AC=6, BC=8, AB=10. A line through the incentre parallel to AC cuts BA, BC at M, N. What percentage of perimeter ABC is perimeter MBN?
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: The triangles MBN and ABC are similar with scale $1-r/h$, where h is the altitude from B to AC and r is the inradius. Also $r/h=AC/P$.
steps: P=24, so r/h=6/24=1/4 and the similarity scale is 3/4. Perimeters have the same scale.

problems.title: A short side creates a right triangle
problems.question: In ABC,∠A=60°,∠B=80°, AB=2. Point D lies on AC and AD=1. Find ∠DBC.
problems.idea: Apply the appropriate algebra, counting, or triangle relation.
formulas: In triangle ABD, use the cosine rule: $BD^2=2^2+1^2-2\cdot2\cdot1\cos60°=3$.
steps: Thus AD²+BD²=1+3=AB², so angle ADB is 90°. Consequently angle ABD=30°. Subtract it from angle ABC=80°.
